data.title: Finatext Holdings' (TSE:4419) Earnings Are Of Questionable Quality
data.description:
Last week's profit announcement from Finatext Holdings Ltd. (TSE:4419) was underwhelming for investors, despite headline numbers being robust. Our analysis uncovered some concerning factors that we believe the market might be paying attention to.

AI is about to change healthcare. These 20 stocks are working on everything from early diagnostics to drug discovery. The best part - they are all under $10bn in marketcap - there is still time to get in early.

A Closer Look At Finatext Holdings' Earnings

In high finance, the key ratio used to measure how well a company converts reported profits into free cash flow (FCF) is the accrual ratio (from cashflow). The accrual ratio subtracts the FCF from the profit for a given period, and divides the result by the average operating assets of the company over that time. This ratio tells us how much of a company's profit is not backed by free cashflow.

As a result, a negative accrual ratio is a positive for the company, and a positive accrual ratio is a negative. That is not intended to imply we should worry about a positive accrual ratio, but it's worth noting where the accrual ratio is rather high. That's because some academic studies have suggested that high accruals ratios tend to lead to lower profit or less profit growth.

Finatext Holdings has an accrual ratio of 0.27 for the year to September 2026. Unfortunately, that means its free cash flow fell significantly short of its reported profits. Over the last year it actually had negative free cash flow of JP¥331m, in contrast to the aforementioned profit of JP¥1.79b. We also note that Finatext Holdings' free cash flow was actually negative last year as well, so we could understand if shareholders were bothered by its outflow of JP¥331m.

That might leave you wondering what analysts are forecasting in terms of future profitability. Luckily, you can click here to see an interactive graph depicting future profitability, based on their estimates.

Our Take On Finatext Holdings' Profit Performance

Finatext Holdings didn't convert much of its profit to free cash flow in the last year, which some investors may consider rather suboptimal. Because of this, we think that it may be that Finatext Holdings' statutory profits are better than its underlying earnings power.
